title: Possessives 2: Ours and Yours (наш / ваш)
description: The 'our' and 'your-plural-or-polite' possessives follow the same four-form pattern as мой and твой. Today we drill наш / наша / наше / наши and ваш / ваша / ваше / ваши.
descriptionRussian: Местоимения 'наш' и 'ваш' имеют те же четыре формы, что и 'мой / твой'. Сегодня — наш / наша / наше / наши и ваш / ваша / ваше / ваши.
intro: Two more possessives, and they should cost you noticeably less than the first two did. That is the point of learning a shape rather than a list: the slots are already in your head, and only the stem is new. Russian will keep doing this to you, in case after case, for as long as you study it. The lesson worth taking from today is not two words. It is that the second set of anything is cheaper.
rules: The possessive pronoun наш ('our') has four forms: наш (m sg), наша (f sg), наше (n sg), наши (pl). Same parallel slots as мой and твой.
The possessive pronoun ваш ('your', polite or plural) has four forms: ваш, ваша, ваше, ваши. Mirrors наш exactly.
The masculine singular has no vowel ending: just наш or ваш. The vowel returns in the other three forms (наша / ваша, наше / ваше, наши / ваши).
The neuter singular ends in -е (наше, ваше), not -ё. The -ё of моё / твоё is special to those two words, not a general neuter rule.
Use ваш for one polite 'you' (a stranger, an older person, a teacher) OR for any plural 'you' (two or more people). Both contexts use the same form.
examples: Это наш дом. (This is our house.) Дом is masculine singular, so the possessive is simply наш.
Это наша школа. (This is our school.) Школа is feminine singular, so the possessive takes -а: наша.
Это наше окно. (This is our window.) Окно is neuter singular, so the possessive takes -е: наше.
Это наши дети. (These are our children.) Дети is plural, so the possessive takes -и: наши.
Это ваш паспорт? (Is this your passport?) Паспорт is masculine singular, addressed to a single polite вы: ваш.
Это ваши книги? (Are these your books?) Книги is plural, so the form is ваши regardless of how many people you are addressing.

tables.title: Наш and Ваш across the Four Forms

items.promptEnglish: Recap from Lesson 1: this is my cat.
items.hint: Кот is masculine singular. Pick the matching form of 'my' from yesterday.
items.explanation: Recap from Lesson 1. Кот is masculine singular, so the 'my' series takes мой. Today's lesson swaps мой for наш and ваш, but the agreement instinct is the same: read the noun, pick the matching ending.

items.hint: Дом is masculine singular. The masculine form of the 'our' series has no vowel ending.
items.explanation: Дом is masculine singular. The masculine form of the 'our' series is just наш, with no vowel ending. Compare with мой from yesterday: both fill the same masculine slot.

items.hint: Школа ends in -а. Which gender takes -а on the possessive?
items.explanation: Школа is feminine singular. The feminine form of the 'our' series is наша. The same -а ending sits on every other feminine -а noun: наша мама, наша работа, наша квартира.

items.hint: Окно ends in -о. The neuter form of наш is which one?
items.explanation: Окно is neuter singular. The neuter form of the 'our' series is наше, with -е (not -ё). The -ё of моё / твоё is special to those two words.

items.hint: Родители is plural. Which form covers any plural noun?
items.explanation: Родители is plural. The plural form of the 'your' series is ваши, and it works for any gender of plural noun. The form ваши is the same whether you are addressing one polite person about their parents or two people about theirs.

items.hint: Имя is one of the rare neuter nouns ending in -я (a small group: имя, время). Treat it as neuter singular.
items.explanation: Имя is neuter singular. The form belongs to a small group of neuter nouns that end in -я (имя, время, племя), but the gender is still neuter. The neuter form of the 'your' series is ваше.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Квартира is feminine singular. The feminine form of the 'your' series is ваша.

errorCorrection.sentence: Это наша дети приехали из лагеря.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: These are our children back from camp.
errorCorrection.explanation: Дети is plural, so 'our' takes the plural form: наши. Наша is feminine singular, so it cannot describe a plural noun. The verb приехали is also plural, confirming the number.

errorCorrection.sentence: Это наш друзья из соседнего города приехали на выходные.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: These are our friends from the neighbouring city, they've come for the weekend.
errorCorrection.explanation: Друзья is plural (the special plural of друг), so 'our' takes the plural form: наши друзья. The plural -и ending is the same for every gender: both 'наши мальчики' and 'наши девочки' use it. The plural verb приехали confirms that the subject is plural.

errorCorrection.sentence: Это ваш квартира на втором этаже.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: This is your apartment on the second floor.
errorCorrection.explanation: Квартира is feminine (ends in -а), so 'your' takes the feminine form: ваша. The feminine -а on ваша mirrors the -а on the noun.

minimalPairs.explanation: Работа is feminine singular, so the possessive takes -а: наша. Наш alone would only fit a masculine noun like дом.
Дети is plural, so the possessive takes -и: ваши. Ваше would only fit a neuter singular noun like место.

reviewVocab.definition: polite form (the вы and ваш forms used when addressing a single person formally; same form covers true plural too)
reviewVocab.example: В разговоре с незнакомым человеком в магазине используется вежливая форма: 'Это ваш чек?'

reviewVocab.definition: plural number (more than one of something; triggers the -и ending on possessives)
reviewVocab.example: Слово 'книги' стоит во множественном числе, поэтому правильная форма местоимения — 'наши книги'.

reviewVocab.definition: pronoun (a small replacement word like я, ты, мы, вы, мой, наш, ваш that stands in for a noun or shows possession)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Это наша школа' слово 'наша' — это притяжательное местоимение в женском роде.
